current_activity: Charnwood: clears the Lebisey area and, with the 33rd Armoured Brigade, takes the high ground round Point 64 above Caen
notes: Event date: 8 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 313, 315). Event definition: On the first day of the attack on Caen the division completely clears the Lebisey area and, supported in the early evening by the 33rd Armoured Brigade, captures the high ground round Point 64, from which it overlooks Caen; patrols reach the outskirts but debris stops them (p. 315); on 9 July it moves into Caen (p. 316). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 313: "At 4.20 a.m. on July the 8th the full force of the artillery came down"; p. 315: "British Division had completely cleared the Lebisey area and, apart from some heavy shelling and mortaring from east of the Orne and a short-lived tank sortie against Hérouville, were not seriously im- peded. In the early evening, supported by the 33rd Armoured Brigade, they captured the high ground round Point 64 and were then overlooking Caen". Location: Lebisey / Biéville-Beuville approach to Caen (existing place PL0040) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the Lebisey approach to Caen, the first objective of the day. Location support: Ellis names the Lebisey area and Point 64 (p. 315).

current_activity: Goodwood: attacks at 07:45 on the east flank and takes Sannerville and Banneville by midday; Troarn holds out
notes: Event date: 18 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 343). Event definition: The division, with the 152nd Brigade of the 51st Division under command and the 27th Armoured Brigade in support, advances at 07:45 behind a barrage; Sannerville and Banneville-la-Campagne, well hit by the bombing, fall soon after midday, Touffreville holds out until the evening and Troarn is still strongly defended at nightfall (p. 343). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 343: "the British 3rd Infantry Division of I Corps, with a brigade (152nd) of the 51st Division under command and sup- ported by the 27th Armoured Brigade, moved forward at 7.45 a.m."; "Sannerville and Banneville la Campagne had been well hit and their dazed defenders could offer little resistance; both were in British hands soon after midday". Location: Sannerville, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names Sannerville as taken by midday (p. 343).
